newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Anaconda share issue raises A$96.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Anaconda share issue raises A$96.4 mln.

text.p: Anaconda Nickel Ltd said on Wednesday that it had raised A$96.4 million from a placement of 25 million shares to institutions.

The company, which is developing the A$900 million Murrin Murrin nickel and cobalt project in Western Australia, had earlier sought a share trading suspension ahead of the announcement to the stock exchange.
Anaconda said the average price of the share placement was A$3.85. The stock was trading at A$3.75 at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), a rise of 3.8 cents on the day.

The company said funds raised by the placement meant it now had total cash and financial resources of more than A$200 million, following a recent A$110 million loan facility led by Natwest Capital Markets.

The share placement was oversubscribed and would be allotted in tranches of 13 million shares at A$4.00 and another of 12 million at A$3.70. The higher-priced stock went to institutions who required fixed amounts with no scale-back.
It said funds would be used to strengthen the balance sheet and provide working capital for Murrin Murrin as well as allowing the development of the company's new dry laterite nickel projects.
The share placement was executed and advised by Pru Bache Securities and County Natwest Securities.
Murrin Murrin is scheduled to come onstream at the end of 1998 and to reach production of 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt in that year.
Glencore International AG of Switzerland, which has a 40 percent stake in Murrin Murrin and a 19 percent stake in Anaconda Nickel, has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel.
Anaconda has plans to expand annual production to 75,000 tonnes of nickel and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned.
